C-RELEASE-SIGN-STAGED-SET.Summary: Fix the two execution defects that make the C-RELEASE-SIGNING-SPLIT staged handoff fail the release lane on every run: on macOS the sign job's repackage step converts the re-packaged DMG onto the exact path the verify step's copy already occupied — hdiutil convert refuses an existing output and the step runs under set -euo pipefail, so the macOS sign job fails every run — and on Windows the staged directory holds files without SHA-256 receipts (the smoke screenshot is saved inside the staged dir and the feed fragment's latest-platform.json never receives one) while both Windows uploads use release\* wildcards, so the Windows digest verifier refuses every run with BLOCK_SIGN_DIGEST_MISMATCH. The fix converts into the sign work dir and replaces the destination atomically, moves the screenshot outside the staged dir, records a receipt for every Windows staged file, and names the files of both Windows uploads; a new execution gate in tests/tools runs the extracted workflow shells — with the workflow's one hardcoded absolute path substituted by a per-test temp directory — against synthetic staged sets and fails on the pre-fix text, and the governance digest guard treats the macOS and Windows verify steps symmetrically.
C-RELEASE-SIGN-STAGED-SET.Problem: Three defects confirmed directly against this tree (release.yml VERSION 3.9.0 at HEAD 97fec630; the file is byte-identical to remote main bb68fd6c; each was reproduced by reading the workflow, and the hdiutil behavior was reproduced on a real Mac). D1 (macOS, release-blocking): in the sign job, step "verify staged artifact digests" (if: runner.os == 'macOS', :978-1011) runs mkdir -p /tmp/release and cp "$STAGE"/* /tmp/release/ (:984-985), so the UNSIGNED staged DMG already sits at /tmp/release/Mark_${VER}_aarch64.dmg when the next steps run. Step "repackage and notarize the staged DMG" (:1113-1132) then sets DMG_DST="/tmp/release/Mark_${VER}_aarch64.dmg" (:1129) and runs hdiutil convert "$RW_DMG" -format UDZO -o "$DMG_DST" (:1130). hdiutil convert refuses an existing output ("convert failed - File exists", exit 1 — reproduced), and the step runs under set -euo pipefail, so the macOS sign job fails on every run before notarization. D2 (Windows, release-blocking): in the build job the Windows smoke step saves its screenshot to $env:RUNNER_TEMP\release\app-screenshot.png (:797) — the same directory that is the staged dir STAGE_DIR="$RUNNER_TEMP/release" (:837, :867). The Windows stage step (:859-882) writes a receipt ONLY for the setup exe (echo "$HASH" > "$EXE_DST.sha256", :881); the feed fragment step (:827-857) writes latest-platform.json into the staged dir (:846) with no receipt. The Windows staged upload uses the wildcard path ${{ runner.temp }}\release\* (:909), so app-screenshot.png and latest-platform.json are uploaded WITHOUT receipts. The sign job's "verify staged artifact digests (windows)" step (:1013-1047) requires a receipt for every non-.sha256 file, so it reports [ReleaseSign][sign][BLOCK_SIGN_DIGEST_MISMATCH] ... no .sha256 receipt staged for this artifact (:1027) and exits 1: because latest-platform.json is always staged without a receipt, Windows signing fails on every run, and the smoke screenshot (written whenever the screenshot block succeeds) rides along as a second unreceipted file. The sign job's signed-set upload uses the same wildcard (${{ runner.temp }}\release\*, :1281), so the signed artifact's file set is whatever the directory happens to hold. D3 (test gap that let D1 and D2 through): tests/renderer/release-governance.test.js pins the digest guard only on the macOS step — the requireVerifyThenSign block (:288-306) locates the verify step with sign.body.indexOf('- name: verify staged artifact digests') (:291), which matches the macOS step first and never exercises the Windows "(windows)" step; no test executes any of the workflow's shell text, so a path collision and a missing receipt were invisible to every structural gate.
C-RELEASE-SIGN-STAGED-SET.Relationship: The defects originate in C-RELEASE-SIGNING-SPLIT: that change created the -staged handoff, the verify-then-sign digest gate and the /tmp/release working directory, and its own trust model — "an unsigned artifact whose computed digest does not match its receipt never reaches a signing key" — is exactly what D1 and D2 defeat (on macOS the handoff never completes at all; on Windows the receipt invariant is violated by the upstream staging itself, not by an attacker). This change repairs the handoff and must preserve the split's boundary byte-for-byte: the build job stays free of environment/id-token/secrets, the sign job stays the sole holder, the verify steps' semantics, markers and exit behavior stay unchanged, the needs chain and the prerelease-lane equivalence stay untouched. Stacking: C-RELEASE-CASK-SIGNED-DIGEST — which narrows the publish-cask download to the signed macOS artifact and adds the fail-closed cask coherence check — is implemented in parallel on the same branch and is committed FIRST; this change's baseline is remote main PLUS that sibling, its BaselineAssertions pin the sibling's markers (# VERSION: 3.10.0, the named signed-artifact download, BLOCK_RELEASE_CASK_DIGEST_MISMATCH, // VERSION: 2.5.0, scenario-40) so stacking is provable, and this change touches no publish-cask step. The two changes are independent in content: the sibling consumes the signed macOS set this change keeps intact; this change widens no trust boundary the sibling depends on. The hdiutil conversion-failure behavior is an owner-confirmed reproduction on a real Mac, recorded here as the defect basis; the atomic-replace shape (convert into the work dir, then mv onto the destination) follows the workflow's existing work-dir discipline (APP_WORK under RUNNER_TEMP, :1080).

Goals.Goal: macOS occupied-path fix (decision 1): the "repackage and notarize the staged DMG" step must not convert onto an occupied path. It converts the re-packaged DMG into the sign work dir — SIGNED_OUT="$APP_WORK/Mark_${VER}_aarch64.dmg" — then replaces the destination atomically: hdiutil convert "$RW_DMG" -format UDZO -o "$SIGNED_OUT" followed by mv -f "$SIGNED_OUT" "$DMG_DST", with a one-line comment naming the reason (the staged unsigned DMG occupies the destination because the verify step copied the staged set into /tmp/release, and hdiutil convert refuses an existing output). Notarization and stapling keep consuming "$DMG_DST" exactly as today, and the sign job's existing fresh-receipt re-emit loop (:1162-1166) keeps writing the fresh DMG receipt. No verify-step byte changes; the re-sign, notarize-app and updater-signing steps are untouched.

Windows staged-set hygiene (decision 2): the staged dir holds exactly the release files, each with a receipt. (a) The smoke screenshot is saved outside the staged dir — $env:RUNNER_TEMP\smoke\app-screenshot.png, with the smoke step creating $env:RUNNER_TEMP\smoke first (the screenshot is run-log QA evidence; nothing in the workflow, the tests or the tools reads it from the old path — verified against this tree: the only other app-screenshot.png matches are frozen historical release-asset names in docs/release-notes/github-releases-archive.json and untracked local review artifacts). (b) The Windows stage step records a receipt for EVERY staged file via a loop over the staged dir using the existing node-based sha256 one-liner (:880), skipping *.sha256 so re-runs stay correct — mirroring the macOS staged loop (:736-741) — replacing the exe-only write. (c) The Windows staged upload and the sign job's signed-set upload declare their files as a path: list (the macOS lanes' existing named-class style, :894-898 and :1265-1272) instead of release\* wildcards, so an unexpected file can never ride along; the artifact names mark-${{ matrix.platform.name }}-release-staged and mark-${{ matrix.platform.name }}-release stay unchanged, as do if-no-files-found and retention. The signed-set list drops the .sig file exactly as the macOS signed list already does (no downstream consumer reads it — prepare-publication's Windows copy_one list :1365 names exactly the exe, its .sha256 and its .bundle, and the feed merge :1328 reads only latest-platform.json).

Source-pinned structure with symmetric digest-guard coverage (decision 3): tests/renderer/release-governance.test.js extends the existing guard rather than duplicating it — the requireVerifyThenSign block (:288-306) is extended so the digest-guard coverage treats the macOS and the Windows verify steps symmetrically: both "- name: verify staged artifact digests" and "- name: verify staged artifact digests (windows)" are located, sliced and held to the same demands (BLOCK_SIGN_DIGEST_MISMATCH marker, nonzero exit, no swallowed comparison, no secret referenced before verification), so a mutation applied to EITHER step's verify block is rejected. The file also gains the comment-blind red-control validator assertSignStagedHandoff(source) mirroring the assertCaskSignedDigest / assertGitleaksChecksumContract precedent (in-memory source mutations only, no network, no tracked-file edits, CRLF-tolerant regexes because Windows checkouts carry \r\n), plus a positive pin test for the macOS and Windows fixes and a red-control test whose in-memory mutations restore the direct convert onto the occupied path, move the screenshot back into the staged dir, restore the exe-only receipt, and restore a wildcard upload — each asserted to throw with a distinct expectation — and the existing in-memory mutation test gains Windows-verify-step mutations proving the symmetric guard.

Execution gate (decision 4): because text pins missed both defects, a new small vitest file at tests/tools/sign-staged-handoff.test.mjs — Node-only (first-line @vitest-environment node pragma, the established tests/tools precedent for subprocess-driving suites, since the vitest lane sets environment jsdom globally), no new dependencies and no network — extracts the run: shell of the relevant steps straight from .github/workflows/release.yml (parsed with the yaml package already in the lockfile and already imported by sibling test files) and EXECUTES them against synthetic staged directories: the macOS verify loop and the Windows verify loop run on every OS with bash against a fake staged set (pass case: file plus receipt exits zero; fail case: a file without a receipt exits nonzero with the BLOCK_SIGN_DIGEST_MISMATCH marker; fail case: tampered bytes exit nonzero); a stage-then-verify case runs the extracted Windows stage script over a synthetic staged dir holding the exe and latest-platform.json and demands the verify loop pass — red on the current text (latest-platform.json unreceipted), green after the fix; the macOS repackage conversion runs only where hdiutil exists (skipped elsewhere with an explicit reason naming hdiutil) against a tiny real disk image created by hdiutil create, with xcrun/codesign/spctl replaced by PATH shims so nothing signs or notarizes — red on the current text (occupied destination), green after the fix. The extracted shell text keeps /tmp/release only as workflow text: the gate applies exactly one declared substitution — the literal /tmp/release becomes a per-test temporary directory under the OS temp root, failing loudly when the literal is expected but absent — so the collision semantics are exercised without ever touching a fixed shared path. The file must FAIL on the current workflow text and PASS after the fix; it lands FIRST (deliberately red) and the workflow fix flips it green, mirroring the boundary-guard-first discipline of C-RELEASE-SIGNING-SPLIT.

GRACE bookkeeping synchronized (decision 5): release.yml's own markup gains the version bump 3.10.0 → 3.11.0 (the sibling's bump is underneath), a dated C-RELEASE-SIGN-STAGED-SET CHANGE_SUMMARY line, and MODULE_MAP sentence appends on the build and sign entries; the governance test file bumps 2.5.0 → 2.6.0 with its dated entry; the new test file gets a MODULE_CONTRACT header in the tests/tools form; docs/release-process.md section 4b gains one or two sentences on the staged-set invariant (exactly the release files, each receipted; the screenshot outside it; the macOS convert-and-replace); .grace/graph/features.xml M-046 gains one dated SummaryDelta and the new test file joins M-046's Tests list; .grace/verification/features.xml V-M-046 gains the next sequential scenario (scenario-41, after the sibling's scenario-40) and a Command entry for the new file.

Constraints.Constraint: ObservedWriteScope: .github/workflows/release.yml (the macOS repackage step, the Windows smoke screenshot lines, the Windows stage step, the two Windows upload steps, and the workflow's own MODULE_MAP/CHANGE_SUMMARY markup only); tests/renderer/release-governance.test.js (the extended verify-guard block, the new validator, the new and extended tests, markup); the new tests/tools/sign-staged-handoff.test.mjs; docs/release-process.md (the 4b section's staged-set sentences only); .grace/graph/features.xml (M-046 SummaryDelta and the Tests list line); .grace/verification/features.xml (V-M-046 scenario-41 and one Command entry). No renderer or Rust product code, no new workflow files, no npm dependency changes, no vitest-config change, no new secrets, and no change to the release-signing or release environments' definitions or reviewers.

Every other byte of behavior stays as it is: authorize-tag, manual-build, prepare-publication, publish and publish-cask are untouched (publish-cask is the sibling's area — this change must not revert the sibling's named signed-artifact download or its coherence check); the verify steps' loop logic, marker and exit behavior are unchanged on both platforms; artifact names, upload if-no-files-found/retention and every pinned action digest stay unchanged; the macOS staged upload and macOS signed upload keep their existing named-class lists; the macOS sign job's re-sign, notarize-app, updater-signing, SLSA and cosign steps are untouched apart from the repackage conversion destination; the receipt re-emit loops on both platforms stay as they are.

The execution gate never touches a fixed shared path: the extracted macOS shells hardcode /tmp/release in the workflow, so the gate applies exactly ONE declared substitution to the extracted script text — the literal /tmp/release becomes a per-test temporary directory created under the OS temp root — and fails loudly if that literal is missing from a step where it is expected, so the substitution cannot silently mask drift; the collision semantics under test are preserved because the verify step's cp into the substituted root and the repackage step's DMG_DST under the same substituted root share it exactly as they share /tmp/release in the workflow. RUNNER_TEMP/STAGE/RELEASE_DIR/TAG are environment mappings into the per-test tree, not substitutions; no other fixed absolute path is substituted because none remains — the remaining steps resolve paths through their declared env vars, and the Windows stage step's relative find target fallback never executes because the fixture pre-places the destination exe. There is no rm -rf of any fixed path: cleanup happens only inside the per-test temporary directory, in a finally block, including detaching any mounted disk image before removal; the file's tests run sequentially (vitest's default within-file order) and nothing signs or notarizes for real — xcrun/codesign/spctl are PATH shims and the hdiutil-dependent case is skipped with an explicit reason wherever hdiutil is absent.

The edit is actionlint-clean; the governance suite's existing pins (boundary guard, needs chain, prerelease equivalence, workflow-wide sign concentration, gitleaks contract, beta-checks gate, the sibling's cask-digest pins) keep passing unweakened; new red controls mutate only in-memory source strings with CRLF-tolerant regexes; the new test file adds no dependency (import { parse } from 'yaml' plus Node built-ins only), performs no network access, and needs no vitest-config or CI edit because tests/tools is an explicit include glob in the checked-in vitest config.

GRACE bookkeeping is synchronized and release.yml remains the privileged release lane — every edit, including comments, rides the governed process (grace lint current → target → final), and documentation comments are not mixed with digest or path fixes in the same breath.

NonGoals.NonGoal: No changes to the digest-verification semantics: the verify loops keep their current shape, marker and exits; no new marker is introduced for the conversion failure; the fix is the destination change, not a verifier change.

No changes to the macOS staged or signed upload lists, no new artifact names, no upload/download shape changes other than the two Windows path lists, no action version or digest changes, and no change to prepare-publication, publish or publish-cask.
No screenshot consumer is added: the screenshot stays run-log QA evidence in its new smoke directory; no upload step, log step or test starts reading it.

No dependency, lockfile, vitest-config or CI-workflow edit: the execution gate runs in the existing renderer-unit vitest lane (npm run test:coverage in .github/workflows/test.yml) because tests/tools is an explicit include glob in the checked-in vitest.config.ts, so the new file is picked up by the lane as-is.

No live tag dispatch, signing, notarization, publication or cask PR is authorized or performed by this change; the first real tag run through the repaired handoff is live evidence recorded in the change bundle after merge, and the pre-fix red executions of the gate (recorded when the gate lands) are the defect evidence.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: macOS fix pin (unit): the "repackage and notarize the staged DMG" step contains SIGNED_OUT="$APP_WORK/Mark_${VER}_aarch64.dmg", hdiutil convert "$RW_DMG" -format UDZO -o "$SIGNED_OUT" and mv -f "$SIGNED_OUT" "$DMG_DST", carries the one-line reason comment containing "hdiutil convert refuses an existing output", still submits "$DMG_DST" to notarytool and staples "$DMG_DST", and the direct form hdiutil convert "$RW_DMG" -format UDZO -o "$DMG_DST" no longer appears anywhere in the workflow; the verify step's cp "$STAGE"/* /tmp/release/ and the receipt re-emit loop are unchanged.

Windows fix pin (unit): the smoke step creates $env:RUNNER_TEMP\smoke and saves $env:RUNNER_TEMP\smoke\app-screenshot.png, and no release\app-screenshot.png path remains; the Windows stage step receipts every staged file via a loop headed for STAGED in "$STAGE_DIR"/*; do writing "$STAGED.sha256" with the existing node one-liner, and the exe-only write echo "$HASH" > "$EXE_DST.sha256" is gone; the staged upload declares a path: list naming Mark_*_x64-setup.exe, Mark_*_x64-setup.exe.sha256, latest-platform.json and latest-platform.json.sha256 under ${{ runner.temp }}\release, the signed-set upload declares a path: list naming those plus Mark_*_x64-setup.exe.bundle, and the wildcard path: ${{ runner.temp }}\release\* appears nowhere in the workflow; artifact names are unchanged.

Symmetric guard and governance pins (unit): the extended digest guard slices BOTH verify steps and rejects, with distinct expectations, a mutation applied to either one (marker stripped, comparison swallowed, verification removed) on either platform; assertSignStagedHandoff(source) is comment-blind and CRLF-tolerant and its positive test — keeps the staged handoff collision-free and fully receipted — passes on the checked-in workflow, while its red-control test — fails closed on in-memory mutations of the sign staged handoff — rejects the restored direct convert, the screenshot back inside the staged dir, the exe-only receipt and a restored wildcard upload, each with a distinct expectation; every existing test in the file stays unweakened.

Execution gate (unit, red-then-green): tests/tools/sign-staged-handoff.test.mjs — first line // @vitest-environment node, MODULE_CONTRACT header in the tests/tools form — extracts the four steps by exact name ("verify staged artifact digests", "verify staged artifact digests (windows)", "stage release artifacts (windows)", "repackage and notarize the staged DMG") with the lockfile yaml parser and executes them with bash against synthetic staged directories, substituting exactly the one declared literal /tmp/release with a per-test temp directory (failing loudly if a step expected to contain it does not) and never touching any fixed shared path; on the pre-fix text the stage-then-verify case exits nonzero on the unreceipted latest-platform.json and the repackage case exits nonzero on the occupied destination — the recorded red demonstrating D1 and D2 executably — and after the fix all cases pass: fully receipted sets verify on both platforms, a missing receipt and tampered bytes each exit nonzero with BLOCK_SIGN_DIGEST_MISMATCH on both platforms, and the conversion replaces the staged DMG with the freshly converted image and runs the shimmed notarize and staple against the replaced path; the hdiutil case is skipped with an explicit reason where hdiutil is absent, and nothing real is signed.

Docs and bookkeeping: docs/release-process.md section 4b carries one or two sentences stating the staged directory holds exactly the release files each with its SHA-256 receipt, the Windows smoke screenshot is written outside it, and the macOS sign job converts into its work dir and replaces the staged copy because hdiutil convert refuses an existing output; release.yml VERSION 3.11.0 with the dated CHANGE_SUMMARY line and the build/sign MODULE_MAP appends naming C-RELEASE-SIGN-STAGED-SET; the governance test file VERSION 2.6.0 with its dated entry; the new test file carries a MODULE_CONTRACT header; M-046 gains the dated SummaryDelta and the Tests list line for tests/tools/sign-staged-handoff.test.mjs; V-M-046 gains scenario-41 and the Command entry for the new file; actionlint clean on release.yml; the governance, action-reference and execution-gate tests pass together.

AffectedAreas.File: docs/release-process.md (4b signing-boundary section, staged-set sentences only)

VerificationIntent.ExpectedCommand: grace lint --path . --assertions current && grace status --path . --with modules --json
VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Green structural pins with red-control evidence: the conversion no longer targets the occupied path (SIGNED_OUT convert plus atomic mv, the direct form absent), the Windows staged set is fully receipted with both uploads naming their files and both wildcards gone, the digest guard rejects mutations of either verify step, and the in-memory red controls each throw. Execution-gate evidence is required red-then-green: when the gate lands on the pre-fix text its stage-then-verify case and its repackage case exit nonzero (the recorded D1/D2 demonstrations), and after the workflow fix the same cases exit zero with the pass, missing-receipt and tamper controls behaving as pinned on both platforms; the substituted-root rule is visible in the gate (one declared substitution, loud failure when the literal is absent) and the macOS-only conversion case records an explicit skip reason where hdiutil is absent. A workflow diff limited to the repackage step, the Windows smoke/stage/upload steps and the markup, the test additions, the docs sentences and the graph/verification deltas; actionlint clean. Live evidence stays external: the first real tag run through the repaired handoff (macOS sign green through repackage/notarize, Windows sign green through the digest gate) is recorded in the change bundle after merge.

Assumptions.Assumption: hdiutil convert refuses an existing output (exit 1, "convert failed - File exists") — reproduced on a real Mac per the confirmed defect report; the fix removes the precondition rather than adding || handling, because converting onto the unsigned staged copy would be wrong even if hdiutil allowed overwriting.

actions/download-artifact@v4 with name+path places the artifact's files directly under the declared path (the sign job already relies on this at :966-970), and actions/upload-artifact@v4 with a multiline path list uploads exactly the matched files — the macOS lanes already use the list form, so the Windows lists adopt an established, working shape; Windows backslash path entries in a v4 list match files under the runner temp as the existing single-path Windows steps already demonstrate.

bash and node exist on all three renderer-unit runner images (ubuntu-latest, macos-15, windows-latest), so the shell-executing cases run on every CI OS; where shasum is absent (non-macOS) the gate prepends a node-based shasum PATH shim so the macOS verify loop's digest tool resolves deterministically, and on a local machine without bash the gate skips the shell cases with an explicit reason rather than failing the suite. The gate file declares @vitest-environment node (the tests/tools precedent) so the lane's globally configured jsdom environment and its setup file do not apply to it, exactly as the existing subprocess-driving tests/tools suites already run.

After the sibling C-RELEASE-CASK-SIGNED-DIGEST lands, line numbers at and below its publish-cask edits shift by a few; every criterion here anchors on stable workflow/test text, with line numbers in the plan's ReferenceState given as remote-main reading aids only.
